stanzas: Nie rzucim ziemi, skąd nasz ród,
Nie damy, by nas zniemczył wróg…
Do krwi ostatniej kropli z żył
Aż się rozpadnie w proch i w pył
Nie będzie Niemiec pluł nam w twarz,
We will not abandon the land our people come from,
We will not let our speech be buried!
We are the Polish nation, the Polish people,
Of the royal stock of Piast,
We will not let the enemy Germanize us…
To the last drop of blood in our veins
Until into dust and ashes falls apart
The storm of the Teutonic Knights.
Every threshold will be a fortress for us…
The German will not spit in our face,
The Spirit will be our hetman,
We will go when the golden horn sounds…

notes: line 1.4: 'szczep piastowy' = the stock (tribe) of the Piasts, the first royal dynasty of Poland.
line 2.4: 'Krzyżacka zawierucha' = the storm (turmoil) of the Krzyżacy, the Teutonic Knights; here a figure for Prussian and German rule.
line 2.3: 'w proch i w pył' = into dust and powder; 'ashes' is used for 'proch', which means dust (also gunpowder).
line 3.4: 'Duch będzie nam hetmanił' = the Spirit will lead us as hetman, the commander of the old Polish army; the verb is made from the noun.
line 3.5: the golden horn ('złoty róg') is the call to rise, as in Wyspiański's play The Wedding (1901).
